title: Experiential Opportunity Operating Model and Partnership Infrastructure

decisionLog.outcome: Reset 2.2.2 to proposition development under Andrew Wright, retiring the inherited delivery steps and resource assumptions while a fresh proposition and discovery plan are developed.

summary: Develops the institutional infrastructure needed to turn King's external relationships, alumni community and philanthropic support into a larger, more coherent and more accessible ecology of student opportunity.
detailSummary:
King's already holds extensive relationships with employers, industry, public bodies, community and third-sector organisations, civic and cultural partners, international organisations and alumni. These relationships are distributed across faculties and professional services and are not yet consistently visible, coordinated or activated as an institutional source of opportunity for students. At the same time, philanthropy has the potential to do more than provide conventional scholarships: it can remove the financial barriers that prevent students taking up opportunities and directly fund the creation of new opportunities with social and educational value.

This deliverable will develop the institutional infrastructure through which those assets can be brought together and used more effectively. Its initial discovery will examine how external relationships are currently held and managed across King's, the staffing and systems that support them, where coordination or investment could improve throughput into student opportunities, and how alumni can contribute as partners, mentors, connectors and opportunity providers. It will also review and consolidate financial support for students undertaking employment-enhancing and developmental activity, with the intention of creating a coherent Student Opportunities Fund focused on low-friction microbursaries and more substantial awards for genuine out-of-pocket participation costs rather than purchasing external courses or provision.

Philanthropy will be treated as a cross-cutting growth engine. Alongside expanding the Student Opportunities Fund, the proposition will explore dedicated philanthropic funding for service-learning and social-good projects. One model to develop is paid project-mobilisation roles for PhD students, enabling them to originate and lead flexible projects with community or social benefit while creating accessible participation opportunities for wider cohorts of students. The intention is to use partnership capability, alumni connection and philanthropic capital together to increase both the supply of meaningful opportunities and students' ability to participate in them.

caseForChange.problem: King's has substantial external relationships, alumni connection and pockets of financial support for student opportunity, but these assets are distributed across organisational boundaries and are not yet consistently converted into a coherent supply of accessible student opportunities. Relationship management, staffing, systems, funding routes and philanthropic activity can operate separately, creating duplication, missed connections, uneven access and underused external capacity.
caseForChange.opportunity: King's can build a stronger institutional engine that connects relationship management, alumni engagement, philanthropy and student financial support. Better visibility and coordination of external relationships can increase the throughput and diversity of opportunities available to students. A consolidated Student Opportunities Fund can remove financial barriers to participation, while targeted philanthropy can also create new opportunity supply, including service-learning and social-good projects mobilised by paid PhD student leads and opened to wider student participation.
caseForChange.whyNow: King's Edge requires a much larger and more navigable ecology of meaningful experience, but growth through separate local relationships and small funding schemes will be difficult to scale equitably or efficiently. Early institutional review creates an opportunity to understand the existing asset base before new structures or investment are designed, while giving alumni engagement and philanthropy a clear strategic role in expanding both opportunity supply and access.
caseForChange.intendedChange: King's moves from fragmented relationship, opportunity and funding activity towards a more connected institutional infrastructure that can generate, broker and sustain high-quality opportunities at greater scale. External partners and alumni can engage through clearer routes; philanthropic capital is deliberately used to expand opportunity and remove participation barriers; and students can access both a richer supply of experience and more coherent financial support to take part.
